title: Purpose of the plans practice
blurb: Explain how the plans practice supports communication and control by defining the what, who, how, where, when and how much.
question: Which practice exists to facilitate communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means of delivering them?

teach.h: The plans practice in one sentence
teach.body: Formally, the purpose of the plans practice is to facilitate communication and control by defining the products to be delivered (the what) and the means of delivering them (who, how, where, and estimates of when and how much) so that the business case (the why) is satisfied. In plain English: a plan tells everyone what will be produced, by whom, how, where, when and at what cost, so the project can be steered against it.

head: Question
What the plan defines
rows: The means and methods of delivery
Satisfied by the plan; set in the business case
teach.caption: The plan defines the what and the means of delivery. The why belongs to the business case, which the plan must satisfy.

teach.body: A plan is a communication tool: it gives the project board, the project manager, team managers and other stakeholders one shared, agreed picture of what will happen. It is also a control tool: once approved, it is the yardstick against which actual progress is measured, so deviations can be spotted early. Progress can only be controlled at the level of detail that the plans contain.

teach.caption: Plans provide the baseline; the progress practice compares achievement with it and controls deviations.

teach.body: A plan is a proposal that sets out the what, where, when, how and who for the whole project or for part of it. PRINCE2 uses four types of plan: the project plan, stage plans, team plans and exception plans. Each is built the same way, starting from the products it must deliver, but at a different level of detail.

teach.caption: Business case: is the project desirable, viable and achievable? Organizing: the structure of accountability. Plans: the products and the means to deliver them.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Westmarsh Water's meter roll-out
teach.body: At Westmarsh Water, project manager Callum Reid is planning a smart meter roll-out. His plan names the products (installed meters, a customer portal, trained fitters), the teams and contractors who will deliver them, the installation method, the districts in order, and estimated dates and costs. The executive, Priya Nair, checks the totals against the business case. Once approved, the plan is what Callum reports progress against each fortnight.

teach.h: The plan inside the control loop
teach.caption: Progress control in PRINCE2 follows a plan-do-check-act cycle. Without a plan there is nothing to check against.

teach.text: A plan does not justify the project. The why lives in the business case; the plan defines the products and the means of delivering them, and must satisfy the business case. Do not confuse the plans purpose with the business case purpose (judging whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable).

items: A plan defines the what (products) and the means: who, how, where, and estimates of when and how much.
The plan must satisfy the business case, which holds the why.
A plan is a proposal for the whole project or part of it; four types: project, stage, team, exception.
Approved plans are the baseline that progress is measured against.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the plans practice: to facilitate communication and control by defining the products and the means of delivering them (who, how, where, when and how much) to satisfy the business case. You can also tell it apart from the purposes of the business case and organizing practices.

A.q: Which is the purpose of the plans practice?
options: To judge whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable
To facilitate communication and control by defining products and means
To define the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities
To identify, assess and control uncertainties affecting the objectives
A.why: The plans practice facilitates communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means of delivering them (7.1).

whyNot.0: This is the purpose of the business case practice (5.1).
whyNot.2: This is the purpose of the organizing practice (6.1).
whyNot.3: This is the purpose of the risk practice (9.1).

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The plans practice defines the products and the means of delivering them in order to satisfy the [?], which explains why the project is being done.
options: project product description
project mandate
quality register
business case
A.why: Plans define the what and the means of delivery to satisfy the business case, which is the why (7.1).

whyNot.0: The project product description sets out the major products and their acceptance criteria (the what), not the reasons for doing the project.
whyNot.1: The mandate is the trigger from the business layer, not the justification that plans satisfy.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and results.

A.q: In the plans practice, which aspect is described as the 'what'?
options: The people who will carry out the work
The methods used to carry out the work
The products to be delivered
The estimated cost of the work
A.why: The 'what' is the products to be delivered; the means are who, how, where, when and how much (7.1).

whyNot.0: The people delivering the work are the 'who'.

B.q:
Which two statements about the purpose of the plans practice are correct?
1. Plans define the means of delivering products, including who, how and where.
2. Plans give estimates of when products will be delivered and how much they will cost.
3. Plans set out the reasons why the project is worth undertaking.
4. Plans set out the business options considered and recommend one.
options: 2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
1 and 2
B.why: Plans define the products and the means of delivering them (who, how, where) with estimates of when and how much (7.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: the reasons (the why) are in the business case, which plans must satisfy.
whyNot.1: Both are false: the why, and the analysis of business options, are held in the business case.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: business options are analysed and recommended in the business case, not in a plan.

B.q: How does a plan support control of the project?
options: It is the baseline actual progress is compared with
It sets the risk appetite the board uses when deciding
It records each decision taken by the project board
It replaces the need for tolerances at stage level
B.why: An approved plan is the baseline; progress is monitored and controlled by comparing actual achievement with what was planned (7.1, 11.1).

whyNot.1: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, set by the business, not by a plan.
whyNot.2: Board decisions are recorded in the project log and the relevant products, not as the plan's control role.
whyNot.3: Tolerances are set for each level of plan; a plan works with tolerances rather than replacing them.

B.q: A team manager asks why the project bothers to share the stage plan with the whole team. Which reason best reflects the plans practice?
options: It lets each team member approve the stage tolerances
It gives everyone a common, agreed picture of the work
It transfers accountability for the stage to the team
It removes the need for checkpoint reports in the stage
B.why: Plans facilitate communication: they give stakeholders a shared, agreed view of what will be delivered, how, when and by whom (7.1).

whyNot.0: Stage tolerances are set by the project board, not approved by team members.
whyNot.2: The project manager remains responsible for the stage; sharing the plan does not move accountability.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports are still produced at the frequency set in the work package.

C.q: A plan states the products to be delivered and the means of delivering them. Which practice does the plan exist to satisfy, and which practice compares actual progress against it?
options: Organizing; and the quality practice
Business case; and the progress practice
Risk; and the business case practice
Business case; and the issues practice
C.why: Plans satisfy the business case (the why) (7.1), and the progress practice monitors and compares actual achievements against those planned (11.1).

whyNot.0: Organizing sets accountability, and quality defines requirements and how they will be met; neither is the pairing here.
whyNot.2: Risk controls uncertainty, and the business case practice does not compare actual progress with plans.
whyNot.3: The issues practice handles issues and changes to baselines; comparing actuals with plans is the progress practice.

C.q: Which is NOT something the plans practice defines?
options: Where the work to deliver the products will happen
Who will deliver each of the products
Whether the investment remains desirable and viable
Estimates of when the products will be delivered
C.why: Judging whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable is the purpose of the business case practice (5.1); plans define the what and the means of delivery (7.1).

whyNot.0: Where the work happens is one of the means a plan defines.
whyNot.1: Who delivers the products is one of the means a plan defines.
whyNot.3: Estimates of when are part of what a plan defines.

C.q: At Ardley Rail, the stage plan shows the products, the teams responsible, the methods, the depots involved, and the estimated dates and costs. Which statement best describes what this plan does?
options: It sets the project's structure of accountability
It replaces the business case for this stage
It records how the products met their quality criteria
It defines the what and the means of delivering it
C.why: Products (what) plus who, how, where, when and how much are exactly what plans define, to facilitate communication and control (7.1).

whyNot.0: Accountability structure is defined by the organizing practice in the PMT structure.
whyNot.1: A plan must satisfy the business case; it does not replace it.
whyNot.2: Quality control results are recorded in the quality register, not the plan.

reteach.title: Think of a journey plan
reteach.question: A family planning a road trip agrees where they are going, who drives, the route, the stops, the times and the fuel budget. How is that like a PRINCE2 plan?

blocks.body: Before setting off, the plan lets everyone agree the trip (communication). On the road, it lets the driver see whether they are ahead or behind and decide what to do (control). The reason for going, a family wedding, is not in the route plan: that is the why. In PRINCE2 the why is the business case, and the plan must satisfy it.

blocks.text: Purpose of plans: communication and control. Purpose of the business case: judging whether the project is desirable, viable and achievable. Keep them apart.

explain.body: The 'what' of a plan is the set of products to be delivered. PRINCE2 plans always start from the products, which is why its planning technique is called product-based planning.

items.label: who, how, where, when, how much

test.q: In the purpose of the plans practice, what does the 'what' refer to?
options: The project's benefits
The products to be delivered
The project's tolerances
The business case options
test.why: The 'what' is the products to be delivered (7.1).

whyNot.0: Benefits belong to the business case and the why, not the what of a plan.
whyNot.2: Tolerances are set for each plan level but are not the 'what'.
whyNot.3: Business options are analysed in the business case.

explain.body: The means of delivering the products are who will do the work, how and where it will be done, and estimates of when it will be done and how much it will cost.

test.q: Which list describes the means of delivery that a plan defines?
options: Who, how, where, when and how much
Why, what, who, risk and benefit
Benefits, risks, issues and lessons
Scope, quality, benefits and risks
test.why: The means are who, how, where, and estimates of when and how much (7.1).

whyNot.1: The why is the business case and the what is the products; risk and benefit are not the means of delivery.
whyNot.2: These are items recorded in the business case and the project log, not the means of delivery.
whyNot.3: These are aspects of performance with tolerances, not the means of delivery.

explain.body: An approved plan gives everyone involved one agreed picture of the work, so the board, project manager, team managers and stakeholders share the same expectations.

test.q: Which part of the plans purpose is served when an approved stage plan gives the board and the teams the same expectations?
options: Control
Assurance
Communication
Justification
test.why: Giving everyone a shared, agreed picture is the communication part of the purpose (7.1).

whyNot.0: Control is about measuring actual progress against the plan and acting on deviations.
whyNot.1: Assurance is the board's independent check, carried out by project assurance.
whyNot.3: Justification is the business case's role (the why).

explain.body: Once approved, the plan is the baseline. The progress practice compares actual achievement with it, forecasts, and controls deviations. Without a plan there is nothing to control against.

test.q: Which statement about the plans practice and control is correct?
options: The approved plan is the baseline that progress is measured against
The plan is approved after the work is done to record what happened
The plan sets the business's risk appetite for the project
The plan is controlled by the quality register entries
test.why: An approved plan is the baseline for control; actual progress is compared with it (7.1, 11.1).

whyNot.1: Plans are approved before the work they cover, so they can be used to control it.
whyNot.2: Risk appetite is set by the business, not by a plan.
whyNot.3: The quality register records quality activities; it does not control the plan.
